To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified two novel ANOS1 and 4 novel FGFR1 variants, all of them predicted to be deleterius and therefore likely to be pathogenic.
we have identified new, yet uncharacterized variants in the ANOS1 and the FGFR1 genes in CHH patients, which expand our knowledge of the molecular mechanisms underlying CHH.
we have identified six novel variants in two classical CHH genes: ANOS1 and FGF1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel mutations in the ANOS1 and the FGFR1 genes in patients with congenital hypogonatotropic hypogonadsim.
the identification of novel ANOS1 and FGR1 variants in CHH patients.
the genetic basis of CHH, which is a rare and heterogeneous condition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the genetic spectrum of monogenic forms of hypogonadotrophic hypogonadisma is still expanding and that we need to keep an open mind for new mutations in known genes and new genes.
ANOS1 mutations are more common in KS than in normosmic CHG and that FGFR1 mutations are more frequent in normosmic than in KS.
the mutational spectrum in ANOS1 is still not fully characterized and the role of FGFR1 in CHH pathogenesis remains to be fully understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have expanded the mutational spectrum for ANOS1 (c.313delT) and FGFR1 (p.R111, p.L655P, p.E723K, and c.374_387delTGCCCGCAC) in monogenic hypogondotropic hypogonadalism.
the identification of novel ANOS1 and FGR1 mutations in a cohort of CHH patients, expands the mutational spectrum and provides further evidence of the heterogeneity of CHH pathogenesis.
we have added two novel ANOS1 mutations and four novel FGFR1 mutations to the list of known CHH mutations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mutational spectrum is still expanding, and the full genetic spectrum remains to be discovered.
even the most studied CHH genes can harbor novel variants and should be screened in every CHH subject.
CHH patients should be screened for ANOS and FGFR1 mutations regardless of their clinical phenotype.
